The definition of validation for machine learning (ML) models is primarily focused on algorithm tuning and achieving an unbiased evaluation of model performance, specifically in terms of selecting hyperparameters to avoid overfitting. In contrast, the validation of medical devices (MD) encompasses a broader scope, aiming to demonstrate clinical benefit, safety, and performance of the entire product as intended for use.

Clinical evaluation plays a crucial role in the validation of medical devices, as it is part of the validation process that systematically generates, collects, analyzes, and assesses clinical data to verify the safety and performance of the device. This ongoing process continues even after a product receives certification, ensuring that the device remains effective and safe in real-world use. Thus, while ML validation is more about model performance metrics, clinical evaluation in medical devices is about confirming that the product meets its intended use and provides clinical benefits.
